description: Per-character lock-on camera tuning: the vertical offset from a target character's feet/location used as the camera's gaze point when that character is locked on.

ID.simple: Row key, normally the character/camera ID referenced by Character rows.
ID.technical: FName primary key of the row (ImportKeyField=Id in the export). The virtual camera resolves the target character's Character::Id_CharacterCamera (Character row +0xD8) against the tables in CharacterCameraDataTables (DTM +0x460); the row's own ID is the lookup key rather than a value read by the consumer.

TargetHeightOffset.simple: Height above the locked-on target at which the camera aims (centimetres).
TargetHeightOffset.technical: double, default 0.0 in the reconstructed row constructor. On target change the virtual camera sets LockOnGazeHeight to this value; if the target is invalid, or no row is found in any table, it falls back to the retail constant 135.0. The value is added to the target's world-location Z when building LockOnGazeLocation, used by the target-camera solver and by camera modes 2 and 3 (and to derive LockOnHeightDifference). Exported retail values are 135.0 for all rows in the available export.

notes: The export contains 46 rows; all observed TargetHeightOffset values are 135.0, matching the built-in fallback.
There is a single table asset registered as 'CharacterCameraDataTable'; the manager appends it to CharacterCameraDataTables (DTM +0x460) after all DataTable loaders complete.
OnTargetChanged is only invoked when the target character index differs from LockOnTargetIndex; changing camera rows for an unchanged target will not refresh the height until the target changes.
Evidence is from reconstructed C++ with cited retail RVAs; no claim is made about byte-identical matching or about Blueprint-only consumers.

usages.detail: Loads CharacterCameraDataTable into the manager's CharacterCameraDataTables array.
Registers the CharacterCameraDataTable primary asset loader name.
Selects the camera row using the locked-on target's Id_CharacterCamera.
Mode 2 lock-on gaze = target location plus LockOnGazeHeight.
Mode 3 gaze and lock-on height difference also use the offset.
